newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil BNDES not to probe Merrill Lynch allegation.
newsitem.headline: Brazil BNDES not to probe Merrill Lynch allegation.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) said there was no legal foundation to warrant a probe by the bank into an alleged conflict of interest involving U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch, which acted as a consultant in the CVRD privatization.

A group of lower house deputies alleged that Merrill Lynch's ownership of South African brokerage Smith Borkum Hare (SBH) gives South African mining conglomerate and expected CVRD bidder Anglo American Corp an advantage in the privatization process.
SBH acts as a sponsoring broker for Anglo American on the Johannesburg stock exchange.
The group of deputies presented a formal accusation to the BNDES and claimed the BNDES was legally obliged to carry out an investigation into the matter.
"There is no legal foundation to warrant the opening of an inquiry," said Claudio Neves, the BNDES legal superintendant.
"The bank has already done what it had to do."
The BNDES has received statements and documents from Merrill Lynch, the Johannesburg stock exchange and SBH explaining SBH's relationship with Anglo American.
Merrill Lynch has rejected the accusations, saying SBH's relationship with Anglo American is merely administrative and not consultative.

It has also denied allegations it acquired SBH specifically to pass on information concerning CVRD to Anglo American, saying it gained control of SBH two months prior to its appointment as consultant for the CVRD privatization.
BNDES Vice-President Jose Pio Borges said the documents received should be sufficient to clarify any misunderstandings and refute any accusations.
A 45 percent block of CVRD voting shares is being sold off at a privatization auction on April 29 for a minimum three billion reais and any legal wrangling could delay the long- awaited auction.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
